* Run it against a **saved client** with `runWithClient`: the client's
hosted\n model selection carries `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the runner applies it\n (and refuses a model that cannot) — se
e [`HostRunner`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/host-runner#reasoningeffort).\n* Build the runner yourself with `HostRunner

` (see the [CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#reasoning-effort)).

## Tool policy

A suite's `defaults.t
oolPolicy` is enforced before the MCP call: a denied tool never reaches the server, the model receives the refusal, and the report
records the block by case, iteration and call id. A blocked call is not graded as a call and is not an executed tool span. A `den
y` name that matches no tool the servers expose is invalid input (exit `2`); an unmatched `allow` is a warning. With no `toolPolic

y`, nothing is restrained.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For the upcoming Inspector eval runner with MCP App view tools enabled, use `view:<n
ame>` in a suite's `toolPolicy.allow` or `deny`, for example `view:make_move`. These names wait until the app renders; plain tool
names keep the validation described above. Assertions and side-effect manifests still use `make_move`. This syntax does not enable

view tools in the local SDK suite-file runner.

## Imported cases

Native and claimed-`exact` imported cases run with no appr
st .mcpjam/evals/imported.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reason \"Reviewed against the upstream

rubric"
```

`unsupported` and `unresolved` cases never run. Approving a native, `exact`, disabled, unselected or unknown cas

e is refused. A local approval is recorded as local evidence; it claims no hosted approver.

## What runs locally

| Capabilit

y | Local behavior |
| - | - |
| Prompt steps (including several per case) | Run as one conversation per iteration |
| Determin
istic assertions (steps and `assertions`) | Graded with the hosted assertion engine |\n| Direct `toolCall` steps | Refused before
anything runs — use a prompt, or run hosted |\n| `interact` steps, widget/render and tool-discovery assertions | Refused before an
ything runs |\n| Gating assertions on tool results or per-call latency (`toolResultContains`, `toolResultMatches`, `toolResultMatc
hesSchema`, `toolResultSizeUnder`, `toolLatencyUnder`) | Refused before anything runs — a local run does not capture tool results
or timings yet. An advisory one is reported as not measured |\n| An enabled gating or required judge | Refused before anything run
s |\n| An advisory judge (including the hosted default) | Not run; the report says so |\n| `suppressedSuiteStandardCheckIds` | Ref
used — a local run has no suite-standard registry |\n\nEvery selected case is checked before any model or tool call, so an unsuppo

rted later case costs nothing. Hosted-only capabilities run with `mcpjam cloud eval run --file <file>`.

## Output

* With `--
format human` (the default on a terminal), a summary: the verdict, each case's gradeable-iteration count against its threshold, fa
iling assertions, not-measured iterations, policy blocks and un-run judges.\n* With `--format json` (the default when stdout is no
t a terminal: a pipe, a CI log, or an agent's shell), one JSON report on stdout (`kind: \"eval-local-run\"`). Pass `--format human
` to get the summary there instead.\n* `--reporter json-summary|junit-xml|html` writes that document to stdout; the human summary
and progress go to stderr.\n* `--out <path>` writes the report atomically (in the `--reporter` format, else JSON) and prints the p
ath.\n\nEvery report identifies the run as local and emulated, carries the source-file sha256, the per-case evaluator hashes, the
selection, the effective model and rail per case and each server's binding source, and states that upload was off. Server headers,
environment objects, command lines and token-bearing URLs never appear in any output, and every credential the run was given is r
edacted wherever observed text (an error, a tool argument) repeats it.\n\nThe unit of a verdict is the **case**; iterations are ev
idence. A JUnit consumer receives a `<failure>` only for a measured failure — provider errors, evaluator errors and interrupted wo

rk are reported as skipped, never as failed assertions.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | The run complet
ed and its decision passed |\n| `1` | The run completed and its decision failed — the only source of `1` |\n| `2` | Invalid file o
r flags, an unsupported local capability, an import/approval refusal, or an invalid tool-policy deny name |\n| `3` | Missing or re
jected model or platform credentials, including during execution |\n| `4` | Setup, connection, tool catalog, binding, interpolatio
n or billing failure, or a report that could not be written |\n| `5` | Inconclusive, interrupted, an integrity failure, or no comp
lete verdict |\n\n`Ctrl-C` stops the run cooperatively: completed evidence is kept, the report is written, and the command exits `

5` — an interrupted run is never presented as a completed release gate. A second `Ctrl-C` exits immediately.

ogin store — and returns the decision and the report. See [runSuiteFile](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/run-suite-file.md).
